decision.question: Does the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD retain recognizable DVD identity?
decision.criteria: Pass if the corresponding object is recognizable as a DVD disc or DVD case from its visible physical form and scene context considered together. Evaluate outline, apparent thickness, surface structure, any central aperture, and contextual evidence jointly; neither white color nor circular shape alone establishes DVD identity. The original rectangular case outline and printed artwork need not survive if the replacement is recognizably a DVD disc. Fail if the combined visible evidence establishes a non-DVD object, or if the target is visibly removed without a corresponding DVD replacement. Unknown if correspondence or DVD identity cannot be resolved from the available evidence. In particular, a plain white circular object without a visible aperture, printing, or other distinguishing structure is unknown unless additional visible cues establish either DVD identity or a non-DVD identity. Missing identifying details alone do not establish failure.
decision.binding: Assess the counterpart of the small printed rectangular DVD item near the source image's center. Establish correspondence using its location and surrounding snow depressions and shadows, even if its outline changes. Inspect the central edited white circular object for DVD-disc or DVD-case structure, considering its shape, surface, apparent thickness, and scene context together. Do not transfer the visible aperture or other DVD features of the separate white disc on the right to this central target. Do not require the source's dark coloring or printed artwork to survive whitening.
